A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoDial research. All 17 pages of v1 and 20 pages of v2, including appendix equations, tables, diagrams and code examples, support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renamed content.

before.justification: v1 reports original STAR and MultiWOZ evaluations, component ablations, prompt-optimization experiments and SGP-TOD replications.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds evaluations of CoDialfree and GPT-5-mini configurations.

M1.justification: v1's prescribed DST/NAP pipeline is retained as CoDialstructured. Section 3.2.1 adds CoDialfree, which lets the LLM design dialogue logic from selected Colang documentation and enables unhandled-intent continuation, without prescribing the structured pipeline or an explicit DST component.

E1.justification: Both versions use STAR, its STARv2 silver state annotations, and MultiWOZ 2.2. STAR's 24 tasks and 13 domains and the single-domain and multi-domain MultiWOZ scenarios remain unchanged. Additional method and model configurations introduce no new task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds DARD and zero-shot IG-TOD to the MultiWOZ comparison. STAR's separately identified AnyTOD NOREC BASE and PROG+SGD XXL rows become one AnyTOD XXL row; its exact correspondence to the earlier configurations is unspecified. Most existing comparators remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds GPT-5-mini configurations with minimal and low reasoning settings. Table 1 also redefines strict zero-shot from requiring no task samples or sample conversations to not having seen the same task-schema architecture. This revises the reported comparison criterion without establishing that retained experiments were rerun; existing metrics and offline evaluation procedures remain.

E4.justification: v2 adds a focused free-versus-structured generation comparison. With GPT-4o generation, GPT-4o-mini dialogue inference and no refinement instructions, Table 2 reports 36.6 versus 56.1 F1. Existing oracle-state, refinement, NAP/DST removal, prompt-optimization and single-domain analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Section 4.2 in both versions reports means over three runs. Neither introduces seed information, dispersion estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests. Additional result rows follow the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 add CoDialfree STAR F1 scores of 36.6 and 32.1, GPT-5-mini results reaching 59.2 STAR F1, and a new MultiWOZ configuration with 37.0 JGA and 70.8 Success. Original GPT-4o-mini scores remain unchanged. STAR's AnyTOD entries also change to a single 68.0 F1 XXL result. These are expanded or replaced result entries, not established same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The conversation-history and state definitions and Equations 1–3 retain their mathematical substance. The state-approximation and prompt-optimization algorithms are also retained. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs, and the new generation paradigm introduces no formal derivation.

C1.justification: v2 makes two generation paradigms a headline contribution. Its abstract strengthens v1's STAR SOTA claim among inference-based models and competitiveness with similar MultiWOZ baselines to SOTA on STAR and being on par with SOTA on MultiWOZ. The introduction and conclusion frame these claims around strict zero-shot task-schema transfer.

C2.justification: v2 adds specific limitations: interpretability is demonstrated indirectly, user effort remains unmeasured, and effective modification may require Colang familiarity. It also interprets CoDialfree's weakness and reasoning-model benefits. Existing DST and multi-domain limitations remain, while v1's API-version reproducibility warning and qualification about non-progressive dialogue structures are removed.

D1.justification: v2 documents CoDialfree's selected documentation, continuation setting and generated-code example. The reported model-access period extends from January–May to January–September 2025. Existing NeMo version information, processing instructions, prompt-optimization sample sizes and code/data access links are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Gupta et al.'s DARD reference and discusses its architecture and prompting requirements. It strengthens the positioning against AnyTOD by emphasizing training on similar schemas and limited transfer to changed structures. Earlier cited literature remains, including material moved into Appendix A.1.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten around task generalization and interpretability. Methodology is reorganized into free and structured paradigms, detailed related work and CHIEF explanations move into the appendix, and dataset-specific results sections become a combined benchmark discussion followed by detailed analyses and ablations.

P2.justification: v2 reorganizes the main tables into a combined STAR/MultiWOZ comparison with interpretability and graph-transfer columns and a separate configuration table. The original prompt overview becomes one panel of a paired appendix figure. New figures show an interpretability code snippet and CoDialfree code; the existing structured-code example, schema and other analyses are retained or relocated.

improvement.justification: The free-versus-structured comparison adds useful evidence for explicit program-structure guidance, and the revised limitations more candidly qualify interpretability and accessibility. Additional reasoning-model evaluations extend investigation of the DST bottleneck. These provide a limited overall improvement, tempered by v2's broader abstract-level SOTA claims, which are less qualified than the setting-specific evidence in Table 1 warrants.
